category: currency exchange rate API (live mid-market rates and central-bank reference rates)

free_tier.stated: Free plan, EUR 0, no card: 1 API key and 10 requests a minute on live mid-market rates; the free request count is a lifetime total that never resets, and the pages read do not publish its size.
free_tier.notes: The docs rate table lists the Free request count only as the word Free on a lifetime period. The next plan up, Small, is EUR 4.99 a month for 5,000 requests a month, reset at 00:00 UTC on the first of each calendar month. Each call costs 1 request, and one call may name many target currencies. A range of history on a free key answers 403 historical_requires_paid_plan. The latest table of any central bank is on the free key. The same pages offer keyless lanes, which have their own record (data-apis/allratestoday-open).

per_object_cap.notes: Many targets in one call count as one request.

egress.terms: not metered in bytes; the lifetime request total bounds what a free key can pull

interface_detail: GET https://allratestoday.com/api/v1/rates?source=USD&target=EUR,GBP with the key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header; csv, xml and xlsx output on table endpoints
chaining: Live mid-market rates for a prototype. The keyless lane in data-apis/allratestoday-open needs no key and carries the daily ECB table and the central-bank datasets.

limits.value: a lifetime total of Free requests that never resets; its size is not published on the pages read
10 requests a minute on the Free plan

limits_note: History: a from or to range, or a time value, on a free key answers 403 historical_requires_paid_plan. Bulk path: none on the free key; the keyless GitHub dataset in data-apis/allratestoday-open is the bulk route.
binding_note: The lifetime total never resets, so it ends the key long before 10 requests a minute matters; its size is not published.

identity_cost.detail: Sign-up by email and password, or Google or GitHub sign-in; no card. The docs say registration has a captcha and an email to verify.

reliability_note: Past the quota the API answers HTTP 429 and does not recover until the plan changes; the docs say there is no Retry-After header and the body carries resets_at.
confidence_note: Read from the first-party docs, pricing, free-API and sign-up pages. No key was created, so the lifetime count and the 429 cut-off were not measured.
